cases.prompt: Start a new Flutter app for iOS and Android that signs users in and uploads media to our cloud API. Before implementation, inspect the repository and development environment and tell me what must be set up.
expected_decisions: The implementation model and target platforms are confirmed from repository evidence or marked unknown
API/auth/toolchain/signing/device boundaries are routed before implementation starts
expected_evidence: Flutter/Dart, iOS, and Android project/toolchain signals are recorded
Secret and signing values are not read or copied

cases.prompt: This is a private Flutter repository. We want Codex to use Dart/Flutter MCP for analyzer, widget inspection, screenshots, and hot reload. Check the data paths and set safe preflight rules before we enable it.
expected_decisions: Local MCP traffic is distinguished from cloud-model, package-network, application-network, and analytics traffic
MCP roots are not treated as a filesystem security boundary
expected_evidence: Analytics, package-network tools, filesystem isolation, accounts/endpoints, and protocol logging are reviewed
No private source or secret value is copied into the preflight artifact

cases.prompt: Fix this nullability bug in an existing Android ViewModel. The project commands, SDK, emulator, architecture, and tests are already documented and working.
expected_decisions: A small already-routed mobile edit does not reopen project preflight

cases.prompt: Refactor an internal backend cache implementation. No mobile client contract, auth flow, schema, or user-visible behavior changes.
expected_decisions: Backend-only internal work does not trigger mobile preflight

cases.prompt: Update the expected iOS snapshot baseline for an intentional spacing change; the simulator and snapshot workflow are already configured.
expected_decisions: Existing visual verification handles the change without reopening mobile project setup

cases.prompt: Add the same media upload capability to our already-configured Flutter iOS and Android apps. The shared requirements are upload, cancel, retry after reconnect, and the same backend error meaning on both platforms. Track any platform-specific differences explicitly.
expected_decisions: Capability parity is defined by shared semantics rather than identical source or pixels
iOS and Android each receive explicit verification evidence and allowed deviations
expected_evidence: Shared requirement IDs cover upload, cancel, retry/reconnect, and backend error behavior
The parity matrix contains evidence for both target platforms

cases.prompt: Android already supports account deletion. Implement the equivalent capability on iOS and prove both clients have the same server-side result, confirmation semantics, failure handling, and observability without forcing identical UI controls.
expected_decisions: The existing Android behavior becomes product-semantics evidence rather than a UI template
iOS deviations are accepted only when shared account-deletion semantics remain preserved

cases.prompt: Add an Android-only Bluetooth diagnostic screen for a hardware accessory that is not supported on iOS.
expected_decisions: A deliberately single-platform capability does not create a false parity obligation

cases.prompt: Before coding, compare dual native, Flutter, and Kotlin Multiplatform for a new iOS/Android product using measurable staffing, performance, native-SDK, and delivery constraints.
expected_decisions: Framework selection is an architecture decision, not a capability parity record

cases.prompt: The feature semantics are unchanged. Regenerate the Android screenshot baseline for a deliberate padding adjustment.
expected_decisions: Pixel baseline maintenance does not trigger product-capability parity

cases.prompt: Our configured Flutter app must process 1080p camera frames at 60fps on iOS and Android. Compare pure Dart/isolate, an existing plugin with native processing, and a custom FFI/native boundary. We have measurable frame-time and memory targets and need to decide before implementation.
expected_decisions: The native/shared boundary is chosen from measured quality drivers rather than framework preference
Data size, crossing frequency, copies/serialization, threading, lifecycle, and both platform verification paths are compared
expected_evidence: Candidate boundaries include only viable Dart/plugin/native/FFI options
Performance evidence is scoped to representative Android and iOS targets

cases.prompt: This Flutter scrolling screen misses frames when rendering 2,000 items. Review the render hot path, allocations, rebuild/copy costs, and measure it on our representative Android and iOS devices before claiming the optimization is complete.
expected_decisions: The current render path is reviewed before escalating to an architecture decision
A shared mobile performance claim requires platform-scoped measurement evidence
expected_evidence: Build mode, device/OS, workload, and frame-oriented measurement are recorded
Debug or web-only timing is not used as mobile release-performance evidence

cases.prompt: Add one validated text field to an existing Flutter settings form. No performance target, large data path, native boundary, background work, or measurable latency change is involved.
expected_decisions: Ordinary Flutter UI work does not trigger performance or architecture analysis without a matching risk

cases.prompt: Before submitting this Flutter feature as complete on iOS and Android, verify the required shared tests plus the Android emulator/device and iOS simulator/device evidence for the changed permission and native-plugin behavior.
expected_decisions: Missing required target-specific evidence blocks a cross-platform completion claim
Web or shared widget-test passes do not substitute for platform-boundary evidence
expected_evidence: The gate matrix records shared, Android, and iOS evidence separately
Unavailable local iOS tooling routes to macOS validation or remains blocked
